contentBlocks.text: Last week you wrote persuasive pieces. This week: comparing how the SAME topic is told in very different genres!

Genre means the category or type of writing — fiction (a made-up story) and nonfiction (real facts and information) are two major genres. The same topic, like firefighters, could appear in a fiction story (following one character through an exciting rescue) or a nonfiction article (explaining real facts about firefighter training and equipment). Name a topic, and describe how it might be told differently in a fiction story versus a nonfiction article.
You just started thinking about how the same topic changes across genres! Tomorrow we'll compare two real passages about the same topic.

objectives: Define fiction and nonfiction as two major genres
Describe how the same topic might be presented differently across genres
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's persuasive-writing work briefly.
2. Introduce fiction vs. nonfiction using the firefighter example.
3. Have the child pick a topic and describe its fiction vs. nonfiction treatment.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's real-passage comparison.
differentiationTips: Struggling: offer a familiar topic (animals, sports, weather) if the child struggles to pick their own
Ready for more: ask the child to name a third genre (like poetry) and how it might treat the same topic differently again
This week uses firefighters as its through-line topic across both genres — set that expectation now
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended reflection activity — check that the child names a real topic and gives a sensible description of how a fiction story and a nonfiction article might treat it differently.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 5 Reading standard RL.5.9/RI.5.9 (comparing and contrasting texts of different genres), opening this week's genre-comparison thread from the course's own description.

generationData.instructions: Pick a topic and describe how a fiction story and a nonfiction article might treat it differently.
